title: Which Kilimanjaro Route Is Right for You?
excerpt: Machame, Lemosho, Marangu, Rongai, Umbwe or the Northern Circuit? Answer four questions and you will know which route suits you.
body:
Kilimanjaro has several main routes, and the right one depends on you. These four questions help.

## 1. How much time do you have?

- **6 days:** Machame or Marangu (six-day version). Doable, but tighter.
- **7 days:** Machame, Rongai or Marangu with an extra night.
- **8 days:** Lemosho. Our most common advice.
- **9 days:** Northern Circuit.

More days means better acclimatisation, and that is the main factor in reaching the top.

## 2. Tent or hut?

Only [Marangu](/blog/kilimanjaro-marangu-route-guide/) has huts. All other routes are camping routes, with tents set up by your crew.

## 3. How important is quiet?

- Busiest: Machame and Marangu.
- Quieter: Lemosho in the first days, Rongai.
- Quietest: Northern Circuit, Umbwe.

## 4. What is your experience?

- First time at altitude: Lemosho, Machame (7 days) or Rongai.
- Experienced at altitude: Umbwe can be considered.

## Our quick summary

| Route | Days | Sleeping | Character |
|---|---|---|---|
| Lemosho | 8 | Tents | Scenic, gradual, our favourite |
| Machame | 6–7 | Tents | Scenic, busy |
| Marangu | 5–6 | Huts | Comfortable, same way down |
| Rongai | 6–7 | Tents | Dry, quiet, from the north |
| Northern Circuit | 9 | Tents | Longest, quietest |
| Umbwe | 6–7 | Tents | Steep, for experienced climbers |

Still unsure? [Send us your dates and experience](/travel-proposal/) and we will suggest a route.
